summary.intent: Triage and address the findings from a /code-review (medium) run over origin/main..HEAD on a change to the semantic crate's React-type base walk, fixing the valid issues in a review round.
summary.outcome: Seven review items were triaged: the assistant made `known &= below_react` explicit, fixed the stale doc-comment wrapping, and made the new test identify csstype by file path instead of interface names and thresholds. It re-proved the mutant still fails the revised test, ran lint and the touched crates' tests, and committed the review-round changes. The extra-RPC cost, silent drop of unknown bases, `names` ordering and `both_lanes` wrapper items were judged acceptable and left as-is.

repo: Relevance-model tests live in crates/semantic/tests/relevance_model.rs and use a `both_lanes` helper, which delegates to a variant that takes `load_dependencies`; nine call sites rely on the wrapper.
`PipelineOptions::default().load_dependencies` must remain `false` for existing relevance tests to stay unchanged.
Resolver changes are expected (per the user's notes) to be checked for time and memory on real corpora such as Chakra and antd, not only fixtures.
Sources never reached by the walk are never in `whole`, so the merge lists them; unreached sources fail in the safe direction.
Repo workflow includes a lint gate, per-crate tests, and mutant-proofing a new test (confirm it fails against a mutation, then restore).

code.finding: The base walk now queries the checker for bases of every React type (`base_types`/`parts` RPCs), pushing entries under both `whole` and `below_react` keys into a linear-scanned `seen` Vec. This is a potential hot-path cost on large projects, unmeasured beyond fixtures.
`known &= below_react` conflated 'below a React type' with 'unproven sources'; it was made explicit in the review round.
The test originally depended on exact csstype interface names and member-count thresholds, making it brittle to @types/react and csstype bumps; it was changed to identify csstype by file path.

workflow: Triage review findings against the code before acting; some are real but acceptable, and some are in the safe direction.
After revising a regression test, re-run it against the mutant to prove it still fails, then restore the code.
Run the lint gate and the touched crates' tests before committing review-round fixes.

friction: The automated review's claims about silent drops and ordering needed manual verification, and several were not actual bugs.
Performance impact of the extra RPCs can't be fully measured with the fixtures alone.
open_items: Measure time and memory impact of the extra per-React-type base RPCs on real corpora (Chakra, antd).
The `seen` Vec linear `contains` scan may need a better data structure if it proves slow.
Consider narrowing the walk to React types that can reach non-React bases like `CSSProperties`.
Possibly collapse `both_lanes` into a single helper with an options parameter.
